newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian banks rise ahead of possible rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Canadian banks rise ahead of possible rate hike.

text.p: Canadian bank stocks rose in heavy trade on Monday on the Toronto Stock Exchange as investors looking for quality issues snapped up their shares ahead of a possible U.S. rate hike on Tuesday, analysts said.

"Under that scenario, the big banks will benefit very well, because their loan losses continue to decline, their efficiencies continue to improve, their major investments outside basic banking area continue to do well," said RBC Dominion Securities investment adviser Ira Katzin.
He said major investors were looking for things to buy ahead of the possible rate hike.

"I think investors are looking for things to buy, actually. And the prudent investors are not being hoodwinked by the market's decline of the past couple of weeks...and they are buying the higher-quality issues," said Katzin.
Royal Bank of Canada led the rally, gaining 1.85 to hit 59.00 earlier in the session before slipping to 58.75 as 658,379 shares changed hands.

Toronto-Dominion Bank was the most active, gaining 1.05 to 38.70 on 1,106,288 shares after its unit, Green Line Holdings (Australia) Pty Ltd, said it offered to buy the shares of discount broker Pont Securities Ltd, for C$3.87 per share.
Bank of Montreal gained 1.50 to 53.00 in heavy trade while Bank of Nova Scotia rose 1.40 to 55.05 in moderate volume.

Canadian Imperical Bank of Commerce rose 1.00 to 67.65, off a session high of 67.90, in busy dealings after it said earlier on Monday it will distribute a 100-percent stock dividend of CIBC common shares for every common share held.
National Bank of Canada, the smallest of Canada's Big Six banks, rose 0.80 to 16.40 in healthy trade.
Katzin said the Canadian banks continue to shine compared to their international counterparts.
"The price-earnings multiples of the Canadian banks are less than those in the U.S. and in the U.K., which makes the Canadian banks good value."
He said a favorable earnings outlook for the sector, combined with "a little bit of a basement" for bank shares, created when several of the banks announced share buybacks, boded well for investors.

"There is the feeling that because of rising earnings over the next couple of years the banks will be able to increase their dividends in each of the next three year by about 8 to 10 percent," said Katzin.
